title: Promote agent-state-mapping.feature with four scenarios on #40
why: new-feature requires Gherkin first; the ticket names the target file and S1-S3, and AC3 (omit currentAgent when no role or status) needs its own scenario S4
rejected: Unit tests only, no feature file
Three scenarios without the omitted-agent case

title: Core takes the current agent's role from the current plan step; the host passes only the raw status
why: host-adapter-boundary.md:83 says role comes from plan.json; core already picks the current step (snapshot.ts:62) and the daemon boundary test bans currentStepId in adapters (boundary.test.ts:23), so the adapter cannot derive the role without a business rule

title: Map initializing and running to running; idle, error and closed to stopped; unknown only for unlisted statuses
why: every status of the #26 list (agent-state.md:69) gets a definite state so unknown means only off-list (AC2); initializing is a live session starting work, error and closed are sessions not working

title: No current agent is currentAgent: null, never an omitted key
why: snapshot-contract.md:37 freezes the rule that absence is null, never an omitted key; the panel zod mirror uses nullable fields
rejected: Optional currentAgent key omitted when absent

title: Raw status enters as an optional third parameter of buildSnapshot
why: additive to the frozen entry buildSnapshot(files, now) (snapshot-contract.md:36); every current caller keeps compiling unchanged; SnapshotFiles stays a set of files
rejected: Separate exported function the host calls itself

title: Status lookup through a ReadonlyMap, exact case-sensitive match
why: a plain object would map prototype keys such as constructor or __proto__ (precedent snapshot-decisions.md:70); a Map never throws on any input and normalising case would guess at host text

title: Mapping lives in a new core/src/agent-state module whose index exports only the display-state type
why: one folder per module with an index.ts (package-exports.test.ts:14); keeping the mapping function unexported stops adapters and the panel from mapping, as the plan reader precedent does (snapshot-contract.md:45)

title: Reuse the existing 'core builds the snapshot' When and pass the World's optional agentStatus as third argument
why: A second When with the same text would be an ambiguous step; the World is per scenario so agentStatus is undefined for every existing scenario and their behavior does not change.
rejected: A new When with different text (breaks the promoted Gherkin wording)
Duplicating the step in the new steps file (ambiguous step error)

title: Classify the null host status edge as a functional note, not a security finding
why: A null status maps to the closed state unknown, never throws and never leaks raw text; the typed parameter makes #41 convert it

title: D1 ruled sound: reuse the existing When step, World gains agentStatus
why: A second definition of the same step text is a Cucumber ambiguous-step error and different text breaks the verbatim Gherkin; existing scenarios get a fresh World so agentStatus stays undefined, and a rename on either side turns S1-S3 red.
rejected: move the When into a shared steps file

title: D2 ruled sound: pin non-text and 100k-char host statuses
why: The spec mapping table names a non-string at runtime; the ['running'] case kills a Record lookup that coerces the key, and null or 42 kill a trim-based normaliser. The 100k-char test title is a separate minor finding, not a flaw in the choice.

title: Rework F2: put the later-started step first and assert currentAgent.role equals the role of the step named by currentStepId
why: Reordering alone makes a last-in-progress bug fail; the direct relation assertion also pins the spec invariant instead of leaving it true by construction. Both fit in one test with no production change.
rejected: Asserting the relation only (still passes if the latest-started step is also last)

title: D3 ruled contested (minor, non-blocking): one fixture order for the latest-start agent test
why: Putting the later-started step first catches a last-in-progress selection but now lets a first-in-progress or steps[0] selection pass, and the role-equals-current-step assertion cannot tell them apart when the first in-progress step is also the current one. Both orders in an it.each, as the currentStepId tie-rule test already does, would catch both.
rejected: sound: the reorder plus the relation assertion close the gap

title: Rework F3: run both start orders in one it.each and lead the plan with a finished step so steps[0] is never the current step
why: Two orders make first-in-progress and last-in-progress selection each fail one row; the leading finished step also makes a steps[0] pick fail both rows. Mirrors the existing currentStepId it.each.
rejected: Both orders without a leading finished step (a steps[0] pick would still pass the latest-first row)
Three in-progress steps per row (more fixture than the two-order rule needs)

title: D4 ruled sound: both start orders in one it.each plus a leading finished step
why: Row 1 expects dev-a so a first-in-progress pick fails, row 2 expects architect so a last-in-progress or last-step pick fails, and the leading finished qa step fails a steps[0] pick in both rows. The role-equals-current-step assertion fails if currentAgent leaves the currentStepId step. Same pattern as the currentStepId tie-rule test.
rejected: contested: one row per order is redundant with the currentStepId tie-rule tests

title: Document agent display state in existing glossary and feature catalog, no new node
why: Two nodes already own terms and capabilities; a new node would add a file and an INDEX row for no new question. Keeps doc files (3) below code files (13).

title: Record #40 agent state as a new sibling node, not an edit of snapshot-contract
why: snapshot-contract and host-adapter-boundary are closed records; the #39 precedent (snapshot-decisions) corrects stale lines in the new node, and the decision is additive, so nothing is superseded
rejected: Edit snapshot-contract and host-adapter-boundary in place
New snapshot-contract node superseding the old one
